_rubric.5: Ship as is. No anatomical artefact anywhere in frame.
_rubric.4: Good. A nitpick of fidelity or setting only. Anatomy is clean.
_rubric.3: Compromised on fidelity, setting or composition. Anatomy still clean.
_rubric.2: ANATOMICAL ARTEFACT - extra or fused limbs, merged digits, phantom claws, impossible joints. Automatic redo regardless of how good the rest is.

_criteria: PRIORITY ORDER, set by Chloe 2026-08-20: (1) anatomical artefacts - any extra, fused or phantom limb, claw or digit is the single worst defect and outranks everything else; it pulls the table out of the fiction and starts the AI jokes. Midjourney has this under control, so it reads as a tell. (2) stray text or invented lettering. (3) fidelity to the Character Appearances entry. (4) worldbuilding consistency - background horses and anachronistic clothing are MINOR, explicitly less bad than a phantom limb. (5) token crop suitability.
_scored: 2026-08-20, against the finished portraits (grain + mount + label), not the raw drafts.

notes.stegosaurus: Limbs verified CLEAN. Wrong head (toothy theropod) and undersized plates only.
notes.ankylosaurus: Detached floating claw below the head. Plus theropod skull and no tail club.
notes.gideon_voss: Background is full of finished figurative SCULPTURES. The doc says he WISHES he were a sculptor and settles for practical woodwork - the image gives him the dream, not the compromise, which inverts the character. No tin star visible either.
notes.utahraptor: Three arms, and a background horse's tail merges into the dinosaur's tail.
notes.thaddeus_marrow: Same problem - a bandit camp with horses picketed behind him. Excellent face otherwise; the fix is background-only.
notes.ezra_calder: Superb character shot - pipe, chessboard, the lot - but Klein signed the plate with a fake cursive signature in the bottom right corner.
notes.beatrice_hargrove: Garbled invented lettering on a sign behind her head. Also lands in the token crop.
notes.lark_vance: Overcorrected: asked for eighteen after the first attempt gave a seven-year-old, and got a woman of about twenty in very short shorts. Doc says 16. The stray pteranodon feathers are gone too.
notes.nell_vance: Overcorrected harder - now reads older than Lark, who is her ELDER sister. Doc says Nell is 13.
notes.big_sal: Characterful laugh, but the cook fire is burning between her knees, which reads as an accident rather than a composition.
notes.allosaurus: Extra forelimb; also a Carnotaurus head crest rather than Allosaurus brows.
notes.iguanodon: Still a toothy predator head and no thumb spikes - the spikes are its single identifying feature.
notes.kentrosaurus: Limbs verified CLEAN. Spikes excellent. Wrong head only.
notes.dryosaurus: Feet fused into a claw-mass, legs merge into a third limb, and NO FORELIMBS AT ALL.
notes.baryonyx: THREE forelimbs on the torso. Otherwise one of the nicest images in the set.
notes.deinonychus: Sickle claw detached and floating beside the arm; the tail forks into two.
notes.carnosaurus: Malformed detached hand near the chain; forelimb count ambiguous.
notes.therizinosaurus: Three hind feet on the ground.
notes.pteranodon: Three legs; only one wing properly resolved.
notes.micro_raptor: Two phantom clawed feet on the chair beside the real ones.
notes.judgment_tyrannosaurus: Limbs verified clean. Lumpy proportions and a stubby tail.
notes.triceratops: CLEANEST dinosaur in the set - and it is the only head-and-shoulders framing. See _finding.

redo.note: Score 2 = anatomical artefact, always redo. Score 3 = fidelity or setting only.

_finding: Anatomy failures are a FRAMING problem, not a prompt problem. Every human is clean: seated, waist-up, hands on knees puts two hands and no feet in frame. 10 of 21 dinosaurs (48%) have limb artefacts, and they are all FULL-BODY shots where four legs, two arms, a tail and claws must all be counted correctly. The Triceratops - the only dinosaur framed head-and-shoulders - is the cleanest of the lot. Fix: frame dinosaurs closer, and raise the batch size so there is something to cull.
